articles.title: Sabalenka crashes out of season-ending WTA Finals after losing to Svitolina
articles.summary: World number two Sabalenka’s season came to a disappointing end after she failed to reach the WTA Finals semifinals.
articles.body:
Elina Svitolina overwhelmed Aryna Sabalenka in the deciding set to seal a ⁠6-3, 3-6, 6-1 upset on Friday and reach the semifinals of the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells, where she will face Linda Noskova.

Svitolina absorbed and redirected Sabalenka’s power effectively, breaking the ⁠Belarusian six times before sealing her first victory over her opponent in more than six years with a forehand winner on her fourth match point.

With the win, Svitolina improved to 2-6 against Sabalenka in their career meetings.

“It was a bit of a roller-coaster match,” Svitolina told reporters.

“I played well in ‌the first set but lost a little bit of rhythm. She played well in the second and served much better. I was really happy with the way I could come back in the third after losing the first game.”

The Ukrainian again did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian and Belarusian players following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine .

Svitolina, the 2018 WTA Finals champion, will face Noskova on ⁠Saturday for a place in the final.

The defeat ended Sabalenka’s season ⁠on a disappointing note.

The second seed won Brisbane International in January and then Indian Wells and the Miami Open in March to complete the “Sunshine Double” but did not claim another title after that.

Sabalenka also surrendered the world number one ⁠ranking to Elena Rybakina at the US Open.

She had entered the season finale among the favourites after Rybakina withdrew on the eve of ⁠the tournament because of illness.

Sabalenka declined to speak to the ⁠media following Friday’s loss.

Earlier in the day, tournament debutant Andreeva continued her impressive run with a 6-2, 6-1 win over fellow Russian Diana Shnaider, her third straight-sets victory of the week.

Shnaider, Andreeva’s friend and doubles partner, replaced Karolina Muchova, who ‌withdrew before the final day of round-robin matches with a gastrointestinal illness.

Andreeva had already secured her place in the semifinals before facing Shnaider and will meet American Jessica Pegula on Saturday.

The eight-day, $10m ‌tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the United States-Israeli war on Iran . The event will be played in Charlotte starting next year.

articles.title: Alcaraz y su raqueta sin cordaje: "Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor"
articles.standfirst: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.summary: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, un innovador en los entrenamientos (Mirra Andreeva confesó que le copia ejercicios en el gimnasio), empezó a trabajar con una raqueta sin cordaje en su vuelta a los entrenamientos tras la lesión en la muñeca derecha. Carlitos, totalmente recuperado ya de la dolencia que le tuvo cuatro meses y medio alejado de las pistas, explica las razones que le llevan a seguir utilizando su Babolat sin cuerdas en el inicio de sus sesiones preparatorias. "Son ejercicios para tocarla o intentar tocarla en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacar la mano hacia delante. Es que aquí la pelota va muy rápida y tienes muy poco tiempo de margen. Si tú intentas jugar como en tierra. de tirar la pelota por arriba, al final te están comiendo. Y estos ejercicios son para intentar sacar la mano hacia delante, para tocarla siempre en el centro de la raqueta, para estar agachado, que aquí la bola no bota tanto. Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor", reflexiona el campeón de siete grandes. A Carlitos se le vio con una raqueta sin cordaje el pasado miércoles en la primera práctica realizada en el Inalpi Arena de Turín junto a su entrenador Samuel López.

images.caption: La secuencia del movimiento de Alcaraz sin raqueta. Joan Solsona

articles.title: Taylor Fritz makes honest admission after winning his first indoor title in Stockholm
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday. The American star, ranked 10th in the world...
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday.

The American star, ranked 10th in the world currently, beat Thiago Agustin Tirante in the final of the ATP 250 event. Fritz was in cruise control in the first set, which he won 6-2, but the Argentine rallied to force a third set and took his opponent to a tiebreak.

Fritz won the shootout 7-3 to triumph 6-2, 4-6, 7-6 and claim his 12th ATP title, ending his 2026 season on a high.

Taylor Fritz reacts after winning the Stockholm Open

"It was a stressful match for sure," said Fritz in his on-court interview after the win. "I felt like I came out, I was playing really well, and then I let some opportunities slip in the second set, and then he played a good game, a really good defensive game.

"I made a couple of mistakes. He's got a big serve; he was playing well. It kind of changed the momentum of the match. I was having a really hard time breaking him after that, and it turned into a really tight war of a match."

Reacting to winning his first indoor title, Fritz said: "It feels nice. I think I've lost a lot of indoor finals, but at the same time I didn't really look too much into it because when I won Tokyo the one year, the whole tournament was pretty much played indoors, so I do kind of half feel like I've had one. But it's good to get that one; now all that's left is a clay title."

Fritz's victory comes after a disappointing end to his Paris Masters campaign, where he came close to beating eventual champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals, but came up short. That loss also put an end to his pursuit of ATP Finals qualification.

"It's really big for me to deal with what I dealt with in Paris," said Fritz. "I wanted to go home so bad; I think anyone would. But I knew that I would feel like a quitter and be a little disappointed in myself if I did that, so I'm glad I came here and made the most of it. I'm playing great tennis, and I get to end the year with a title."

This year marked the first time in three years that Fritz has failed to qualify for the ATP Finals.
